neighbours.label: a place name right after 'from' in a journey from one place to another
fire: It once took a week to ride by wagon from Memphis to Natchez.
The old mail coach ran from Knoxville to Asheville.
Back then a trip by steamboat from Louisville to Cairo took days.
Riders changed horses on the way from Denver to Cheyenne.
Imagine going by mule from Santa Fe to Taos in winter.
A narrow road led from Nashville to Chattanooga in those years.
The canal boat crept from Albany to Buffalo all summer.
Early settlers walked from Richmond to Lexington with their cattle.
quiet: It once took a week to ride a wagon around Memphis in the rain.
The old mail coach is kept in a barn at Knoxville.
Back then a steamboat in Louisville cost a great deal of money.
Riders changed horses at the stable in Denver every day.
Imagine living in a mud house in Santa Fe in winter.
A narrow road was built in Nashville in those years.
The canal boat was repaired at Albany over the summer.
Early settlers in Richmond raised cattle and tobacco.
